meta: Asked AI for a caption and it came out stiff like an official letter? Don't describe the tone, give examples. Mark and Bit show you few-shot prompting: zero-shot means no examples, so AI guesses an average tone.

muc.title: AI writes in the wrong voice
muc.text: Mark asks AI to write a caption for selling cakes, and it comes out stiff like a government notice. Bit says: don't describe the tone, give examples.

muc.title: No examples: AI guesses
muc.text: Asking without examples is called zero-shot. AI has to guess what you want, so it gives you an average, safe tone.

muc.title: Two or three examples is enough
muc.text: Few-shot means giving a few sample examples. Paste two or three old captions you like, then write: write one more like these for the new cake. AI picks up the tone, the length, even how you use emoji.

muc.title: AI is great at copying patterns
muc.text: Because AI is a machine that guesses the next word, as in video 7. When it sees a repeated pattern, it follows that exact pattern.

muc.title: Examples should be different
muc.text: Tip: your examples should have different topics but the same tone. If all three are nearly identical, AI will copy them almost word for word.

muc.title: Not just captions
muc.text: This works for customer reply emails, sorting feedback into good and bad, or naming products.

muc.title: Paste 3 examples you like
muc.text: Find three pieces you wrote and liked, paste them before your request, then compare with the result without examples.
